questions.question: How many types of emergencies are provided in the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Emergency (Article 352)**: This is proclaimed by the **President of India** when the security of the country or any part thereof is threatened by **war**, **external aggression**, or **armed rebellion**. It requires the written recommendation of the **Union Cabinet** and must be approved by **Parliament** within one month by a **special majority**.
 
• **State Emergency or President’s Rule (Article 356)**: This is imposed when the **President**, on receipt of a report from the **Governor** or otherwise, is satisfied that the state government cannot be carried on in accordance with the **Constitution**. It is also known as **Constitutional Emergency** and must be approved by Parliament within two months by a **simple majority**.
 
• **Financial Emergency (Article 360)**: The **President** can declare this if the **financial stability** or credit of India is threatened. While this provision exists to protect the national economy, it has **never been invoked** in the history of independent India, not even during the economic crisis of 1991.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part XVIII of the Constitution**:

 
 
• This part contains **Articles 352 to 360**, which outline the emergency provisions designed to safeguard the **sovereignty, unity, and integrity** of the nation.
 
• The **44th Amendment Act (1978)** introduced significant safeguards, such as replacing the term **'internal disturbance'** with **'armed rebellion'** for National Emergencies.
 
• During a **National Emergency**, the **Fundamental Rights** under **Article 19** are automatically suspended, and the President can suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement of other rights, except **Articles 20 and 21**.
 
• Under **Article 356**, the **President** assumes the functions of the **State Government**, and the powers of the State Legislature are exercised by or under the authority of **Parliament**.
 
• The **38th Amendment Act (1975)** made the declaration of emergency non-justiciable, but this was subsequently reversed by the **44th Amendment Act**, allowing for **judicial review**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the permanent nature of the Rajya Sabha?

options.text: It can be dissolved by the President.
The Prime minister can dissolve it.
One-third of its members retire every two years.
It is dissolved every six years.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-third of its members retire every two years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** is a **permanent body** according to the **Constitution of India** and is not subject to **dissolution** by the **President**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• There is no constitutional provision that grants the **Prime Minister** the authority to dissolve the **Council of States**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• To ensure legislative continuity as a **Continuing Chamber**, the law mandates that **one-third** of the total members of the house shall retire every **second year**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• While the **Lok Sabha** is dissolved every five years, the Rajya Sabha remains in existence, although its individual members serve a term of **six years**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Basis**:

 
 
• **Article 83(1)** explicitly states that the Council of States shall not be subject to dissolution, but nearly as may be, one-third of the members shall retire as soon as may be on the expiration of every second year.
 
• The **Representation of the People Act, 1951** further details the term of office for members of the Rajya Sabha as **six years**.
 
 
 
• **Leadership and Composition**:
 
 
• **Vice-President of India** is the **Ex-officio Chairman** of the Rajya Sabha, while a **Deputy Chairman** is elected from among its members.
 
• The maximum strength of the house is **250**, of which **12 members** are nominated by the **President** for their contributions to **Art, Literature, Science, and Social Service**.
 
• The remaining members are elected by the **Elected Members** of the **Legislative Assemblies** of the States and Union Territories through **Proportional Representation**.

questions.question: What is the traditional attire worn by women performing Bihu dance?

options.text: Mekhela Chador (a traditional Assamese dress) with bright colors and jewelry

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mekhela Chador (a traditional Assamese dress) with bright colors and jewelry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bihu dance** is the most popular folk dance of the Indian state of **Assam**, performed to celebrate the arrival of the spring season and the **Assamese New Year**.
 
• Female dancers traditionally wear the **Mekhela Chador**, a two-piece attire unique to the region, which is draped in a specific style to allow for the rhythmic and energetic movements of the dance.
 
• The **Mekhela** is a cylindrical cloth that is folded into pleats and tucked into the waist, while the **Chador** is a long fabric draped over the shoulder.
 
• The most authentic version of this attire is made from **Muga Silk**, which is globally renowned for its natural **golden sheen** and high durability.
 
• The outfit is characterized by its vibrant **Assamese motifs**, often featuring floral designs and traditional borders in contrasting colors like red and gold.
 
• Traditional accessories are essential to the performance, including **Assamese jewelry** such as **Gaam-Kharu** (broad bracelets), **Jonbir** (crescent-shaped necklace), and the **Kopou Phul** (foxtail orchid) placed in the hair.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Silk Varieties of Assam**:

 
 
• **Muga Silk**: Produced by the silkworm **Antheraea assamensis**, it has a **Geographical Indication (GI)** tag and is exclusive to Assam.
 
• **Pat Silk**: A white or off-white mulberry silk used for making formal and festive **Mekhela Chadors**.
 
• **Eri Silk**: Known as the 'silk of peace', it is processed without killing the pupae and provides warmth.
 
 
 
• **Musical Elements**:
 
 
• The dance is accompanied by the **Bihu Dhol** (drum), the **Pepa** (an instrument made from **Buffalo Horn**), and the **Gogona** (a bamboo jaw harp).
 
• Performers also use **Tala** (cymbals) and **Banh-hi** (bamboo flute) to create the distinctive upbeat rhythm.
 
 
 
• **Male Attire**:
 
 
• Male dancers wear a **Dhoti** and **Gamocha** (traditional handwoven cloth with red patterns) around the head and waist.

questions.question: In what year was the German Expressionist artist group "Die Brücke" founded?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1905**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Die Brücke** (The Bridge) was a major group of **German Expressionist** artists formed on **June 7, 1905**, in the city of **Dresden**.
 
• The group was established by four architecture students at the **Dresden Technical University**: **Ernst Ludwig Kirchner**, **Fritz Bleyl**, **Erich Heckel**, and **Karl Schmidt-Rottluff**.
 
• The name was inspired by a passage from **Friedrich Nietzsche’s** 'Thus Spoke Zarathustra', symbolizing the artists' desire to serve as a bridge between the art of the past and the **modern avant-garde**.
 
• In **1906**, the group published a **manifesto** carved in wood, which declared their intent to achieve freedom of life and movement against established older forces.
 
• The artists are renowned for their **bold**, **non-naturalistic colors** and jagged, simplified forms that sought to convey powerful psychological and emotional states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Development and Membership**:

 
 
• Other significant artists joined the group later, including **Emil Nolde** and **Max Pechstein** in **1906**, and **Otto Mueller** in **1910**.
 
• The group shared a communal studio and developed a uniform collective style, heavily influenced by **Primitivism** and the **Post-Impressionism** of **Vincent van Gogh** and **Paul Gauguin**.
 
 
 
• **Relocation and Dissolution**:
 
 
• In **1911**, the members moved to **Berlin**, where their work began to reflect the alienation and frantic energy of the modern metropolis.
 
• The group formally dissolved in **1913** following internal disagreements, particularly over **Kirchner’s** publication of the **Chronik der Brücke**, which other members felt exaggerated his personal role.
 
 
 
• **Artistic Legacy**:
 
 
• **Die Brücke** is credited with reviving the **woodcut** as a vital artistic medium, using its raw, coarse qualities to emphasize **Expressionist** themes.
 
• Their work laid the foundation for **20th-century modernism** in **Germany**, preceding and influencing the **Der Blaue Reiter** movement.

questions.question: The "Great Nicobar Island" is closest to which neighboring country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indonesia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Great Nicobar Island** is the southernmost and largest of the **Nicobar Islands** in India, situated at the southern end of the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• The island is separated from the **Indonesian** island of **Sumatra** by the **Six Degree Channel**, which is a major international shipping lane.
 
• The geographical distance between **Indira Point** (the southernmost tip of Great Nicobar) and **Rondo Island** of **Indonesia** is approximately **145 to 150 kilometers** (90 miles).
 
• While **Myanmar** is the closest neighbor to the **Andaman** group of islands (specifically near the **Coco Channel**), it is significantly further from the **Nicobar** group compared to **Sumatra**.
 
• **Sri Lanka** is located to the west of the islands and **Bangladesh** to the north, both situated over **1,000 kilometers** away from the Great Nicobar coast.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indira Point:**

 
 
• Located on Great Nicobar, it is the **southernmost point** of the **Indian Union** territory, situated at **6°45'N latitude**.
 
• It was previously known as **Pygmalion Point** and **Parsons Point** before being renamed in honor of **Indira Gandhi**.
 
 
 
• **Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve:**
 
 
• The island is home to a **UNESCO World Biosphere Reserve**, protecting unique species like the **Nicobar Megapode** and the **Giant Robber Crab**.
 
• It encompasses the **Galathea National Park** and the **Campbell Bay National Park**.
 
 
 
• **Six Degree Channel:**
 
 
• This channel represents the **maritime boundary** between India and **Indonesia**.
 
• It is a vital strategic corridor connecting the **Andaman Sea** to the **Indian Ocean** and leads toward the **Strait of Malacca**.

questions.question: Who is regarded as the first woman martyr and a suicide bomber in Indian history, serving as a commander under Queen Velu Nachiyar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuyili**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kuyili** was a valiant **18th-century** warrior and the commander-in-chief of the female wing of **Queen Velu Nachiyar**’s army, known as the **Udaiyaal**.
 
• She is historically celebrated as the **first woman martyr** and the **first recorded suicide bomber** in the Indian struggle against colonial rule.
 
• In **1780**, during a decisive battle to reclaim the kingdom of **Sivaganga** from the **British East India Company** and the **Nawab of Arcot**, she executed a strategic suicide mission.
 
• Kuyili doused herself in **ghee** and **oil**, set herself on fire, and walked into the **ammunition dump** of the British located within the **Kottai Mariamman Temple**.
 
• The resulting explosion completely destroyed the British armory, providing the tactical advantage needed for **Velu Nachiyar** to defeat the forces and regain her throne.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Queen Velu Nachiyar**:

 
 
• Known as **Veeramangai** (Brave Woman), she was the **Queen of Sivaganga** and the first Indian queen to wage a successful war against the **British East India Company**.
 
 
 
• **Jhalkari Bai**:
 
 
• A prominent warrior in **Rani Lakshmibai**’s army during the **Revolt of 1857**. She was a master of disguise who frequently posed as the Queen to facilitate the Queen’s escape from **Jhansi Fort**.
 
 
 
• **Lakshmi Sahgal**:
 
 
• A revolutionary officer of the **Indian National Army (INA)** and the Minister of Women’s Affairs in the **Azad Hind government**. She led the all-female **Rani of Jhansi Regiment**.
 
 
 
• **Matangini Hazra**:
 
 
• An Indian revolutionary affectionately known as **Gandhi Buri**. She was shot dead by British police in **1942** while leading a procession during the **Quit India Movement** in Tamluk, Bengal.

questions.question: If the star is similar to the Sun, what can be inferred about the exoplanet's surface temperature compared to Earth?

options.text: No effect of distance on temperature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Similar temperature**__.

 

__Key Points__

__
 
• The Sun is classified as a **G-type main-sequence star** (G2V), characterized by an effective surface temperature of approximately **5,778 K**. If an exoplanet orbits a star of the same spectral class, the **Stellar Luminosity** (total energy output) remains nearly identical to that of our Sun.
 
• Surface temperature is primarily governed by **Stellar Flux**, which follows the **Inverse Square Law**. This law states that the intensity of radiation is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the source.
 
• For an exoplanet to have a **Similar temperature** to Earth, it must be located within the **Circumstellar Habitable Zone** (CHZ). In a solar analog system, this zone is situated at an **Orbital Radius** of roughly **1 Astronomical Unit (AU)**.
 
• At **1 AU** from a Sun-like star, a planet receives an **Insolation** (solar constant) of about **1,361 Watts per square meter**. If the exoplanet possesses an **Atmospheric Composition** and **Bond Albedo** (reflectivity) comparable to Earth, its **Radiative Equilibrium** will result in similar thermal conditions.

Additional Information__

 
• **Factors Affecting Planetary Temperature**:

 
 
• **Greenhouse Effect**: Even with similar stellar flux, a dense atmosphere rich in **Carbon Dioxide** or **Methane** can lead to extreme heating, as seen on **Venus**.
 
• **Albedo**: A planet with high ice cover reflects more **Shortwave Radiation**, potentially leading to a **Cooler** surface despite being in the habitable zone.
 
• **Stellar Classification**:
 
 
• **M-Dwarfs (Red Dwarfs)**: These are much cooler than the Sun; planets must orbit much closer to achieve Earth-like temperatures, often becoming **Tidally Locked**.
 
• **O or B Type Stars**: These are massive and hot, pushing the habitable zone much further out into the star system.
 
 
 
• **Stefan-Boltzmann Law**: This principle explains that the power radiated per unit area of a **Black Body** is proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature, a critical factor in calculating **Planetary Equilibrium Temperature**.

questions.question: Which temple is known for its unique architecture combining Hindu and Islamic styles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Laxmi Narayan Temple, Orchha**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Laxmi Narayan Temple**, situated in **Orchha**, **Madhya Pradesh**, was constructed in **1622** by **Raja Vir Singh Deo** of the **Bundela Dynasty**.
 
• The temple is distinguished by its **eclectic architectural style**, which represents a rare fusion of **Hindu temple design** and **Islamic (Mughal) elements**.
 
• Architecturally, the building is unique for its **triangular ground plan** and **fortress-like exterior**, featuring **octagonal bastions** and **cannon slots**, which were atypical for traditional Hindu shrines.
 
• The **Islamic influence** is prominently seen in the use of **pointed arches**, **domed rooftops**, and **symmetrical geometric patterns** on the ceilings and walls.
 
• Internally, the temple is renowned for its **Bundela school of painting**; these **frescoes** depict diverse subjects ranging from the **Ramayana** and **Lord Krishna** to the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**.
 
• This synthesis reflects the **Indo-Islamic cultural integration** prevalent in the **Bundelkhand region** during the 17th century, where local rulers incorporated **Mughal aesthetics** into religious structures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Qutb Minar**:

 
 
• Located in **Delhi**, this **UNESCO World Heritage Site** is a **73-meter minaret** commissioned by **Qutb-ud-din Aibak**.
 
• While it is a primary example of **Indo-Islamic architecture**, it is a **tower** and not a Hindu temple.
 
 
 
• **Sun Temple, Konark**:
 
 
• A **13th-century** temple in **Odisha** built by **King Narasimhadeva I** of the **Eastern Ganga Dynasty**.
 
• It follows the **Kalinga architectural style**, designed as a colossal **chariot** for the **Sun God (Surya)** with **24 stone wheels**.
 
 
 
• **Sanchi Stupa**:
 
 
• Commissioned by **Emperor Ashoka** in the **3rd century BCE**, this site in **Madhya Pradesh** is a landmark of **Buddhist architecture**.
 
• The structure is characterized by its **hemispherical dome** and intricate **Toranas** (gateways) carved with **Jataka tales**.

questions.question: What causes the precession of the Earth's axis?

options.text: Gravitational pull of the Sun and Moon

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gravitational pull of the Sun and Moon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Earth is not a perfect sphere but an **oblate spheroid**, characterized by a distinct **equatorial bulge** caused by its rotation.
 
• **Axial precession**, also known as the precession of the equinoxes, is primarily caused by the **gravitational forces** of the **Moon** and the **Sun** acting upon this equatorial bulge.
 
• Because the Earth's rotational axis is tilted at an angle of approximately **23.5 degrees** relative to the **ecliptic plane** (the plane of Earth's orbit), the gravitational pull of these celestial bodies creates a **torque**.
 
• This torque attempts to pull the Earth's axis into a perpendicular orientation relative to the ecliptic, but due to the Earth's **angular momentum** (rotation), the axis instead precesses like a spinning top.
 
• The Earth's axis completes one full circle of precession approximately every **25,800 years**, causing the position of the **North Star** to change over long geological periods; for instance, **Vega** was the North Star around 12,000 BCE and will be again in roughly 12,000 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Milankovitch Cycles**: Precession is a critical component of these cycles, which describe the collective effects of changes in the Earth's movements on its climate over thousands of years.

 
 
• **Obliquity**: Refers to the change in the angle of Earth's axial tilt, which varies between **22.1 and 24.5 degrees** over a 41,000-year cycle.
 
• **Eccentricity**: Describes the variation in the shape of Earth's orbit around the Sun, changing from nearly circular to slightly elliptical over 100,000-year intervals.
 
 
 
• **Solar Winds**: These are streams of **charged particles** (plasma) ejected from the Sun's upper atmosphere. While they cause **geomagnetic storms** and **auroras**, they have no significant impact on the mechanical orientation of Earth's axis.
 
• **Nutation**: This is a small, periodic 'wobbling' superimposed on the larger precessional motion, largely caused by the specific **tidal forces** and the 18.6-year cycle of the Moon's nodes.

questions.question: Which of the following countries was the first to win the FIBA Basketball World Cup after it was established in 1950?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Argentina**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The inaugural **FIBA World Championship** (now known as the **FIBA Basketball World Cup**) was held in **1950** following a decision by the **FIBA Congress** during the **1948 London Olympics**.
 
• **Argentina** was selected as the host nation for the first edition, with all matches taking place at the **Luna Park Stadium** in **Buenos Aires**.
 
• A total of **ten nations** participated in the tournament, including teams from **South America**, **North America**, and **Europe**.
 
• The championship was decided through a final round-robin stage rather than a single knockout game; however, the match between **Argentina** and the **United States** on **November 3, 1950**, served as the de facto final.
 
• **Argentina** emerged victorious by defeating the **United States** with a score of **64−50**, securing the first-ever gold medal in the tournament's history.
 
• **Oscar Furlong**, a key player for the Argentine team, was the leading scorer of the final and was subsequently named the tournament's **Most Valuable Player (MVP)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **United States**:

 
 
• In the **1950** tournament, the U.S. was represented by the **Denver Chevrolets**, an **Amateur Athletic Union (AAU)** team.
 
• They finished the competition as the **silver medalists** after their loss to the host nation.
 
 
 
• **Brazil**:
 
 
• Brazil finished in **fourth place** during the inaugural **1950** event.
 
• They later became a dominant force in international basketball, winning consecutive world titles in **1959** and **1963**.
 
 
 
• **Chile**:
 
 
• Chile performed exceptionally well in the first edition, securing the **bronze medal** (third place) after defeating Brazil in the final round.
 
 
 
• **Tournament Evolution**:
 
 
• The competition was renamed the **FIBA Basketball World Cup** starting with the **2014 edition** held in Spain.
 
• The **Naismith Trophy**, awarded to the champion, is named after **James Naismith**, the inventor of basketball.

questions.question: What does FIDE stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Federation Internationale des Echecs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **FIDE** is the standard acronym for the **Fédération Internationale des Échecs**, which translates from French to English as the **International Chess Federation** or **World Chess Federation**.
 
• It serves as the international governing body for the sport of **chess**, regulating all international chess competitions and overseen by the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)**.
 
• The organization was officially founded on **July 20, 1924**, in **Paris, France**, during the first unofficial **Chess Olympiad**.
 
• Its primary role includes defining the **Laws of Chess**, calculating **Elo ratings** for players, and organizing high-level tournaments such as the **World Chess Championship**.
 
• The official motto of FIDE is **'Gens una sumus'**, which is a Latin phrase meaning **'We are one people'**, emphasizing global unity through the game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Organizational Structure and Titles**:

 
 
• FIDE is responsible for awarding prestigious international titles based on performance, including **Grandmaster (GM)**, **International Master (IM)**, **FIDE Master (FM)**, and **Candidate Master (CM)**.
 
• The administrative headquarters of the federation are currently located in **Lausanne, Switzerland**, known as the **Olympic Capital**.
 
 
 
• **Major Tournaments**:
 
 
• It conducts the biennial **Chess Olympiad**, where teams representing various nations compete against each other.
 
• It manages the **Candidates Tournament**, a critical event that determines the challenger who will play against the reigning **World Chess Champion**.
 
• The organization currently comprises over **190 national chess federations** as member affiliates.

questions.question: Cork cells contain which substance in their cell walls that makes them impermeable to gases and water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Suberin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cork cells**, also known as phellem, constitute the outermost protective layer of the **bark** in woody plants, replacing the epidermis during secondary growth.
 
• These cells are characterized by the heavy deposition of a complex, waxy biopolymer called **Suberin** within their cell walls.
 
• **Suberin** is highly **hydrophobic** (water-repellent), which acts as a chemical barrier preventing the movement of water and dissolved solutes across the tissue.
 
• The accumulation of this substance makes the cell walls **impermeable** to **gases** and **water**, effectively sealing off the plant's internal tissues from environmental stress and desiccation.
 
• Due to this impermeability, mature cork cells become **dead** as they lose the ability to exchange essential nutrients and gases with their surroundings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cutin**:

 
 
• It is a polyester of hydroxy fatty acids found primarily in the **plant cuticle** covering the epidermis of leaves and young stems.
 
• Its primary role is to restrict **transpiration** and provide protection against ultraviolet radiation and pathogens.
 
 
 
• **Lignin**:
 
 
• A complex organic polymer that provides **mechanical strength** and structural rigidity to the secondary cell walls of vascular plants.
 
• It is a vital component of **Xylem** vessels, allowing plants to grow tall and transport water under tension without the vessels collapsing.
 
 
 
• **Cellulose**:
 
 
• The most abundant organic polymer on Earth, consisting of linear chains of **β-glucose** units.
 
• It provides **tensile strength** to the primary cell wall, maintaining the structural integrity and shape of plant cells.

questions.question: How many membranes surround a mitochondrion?

questions.question: Which Indian state has the largest forest cover by area?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2021**, **Madhya Pradesh** continues to hold the largest forest cover in India by area.
 
• The total forest area in **Madhya Pradesh** is **77,493 square kilometers**, which represents approximately **25.14%** of the state's total geographical territory.
 
• This assessment is conducted biennially by the **Forest Survey of India (FSI)**, an organization under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**, using **LISS-III** satellite data.
 
• The state’s vast forest resources are categorized into **Reserved**, **Protected**, and **Unclassified forests**, housing significant **Tiger Reserves** such as **Kanha**, **Panna**, and **Pench**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arunachal Pradesh**:

 
 
• Ranks second in India in terms of forest area with **66,431 square kilometers**.
 
• In terms of percentage of its own geographical area, it boasts a high density of **79.33%**.
 
 
 
• **Chhattisgarh**:
 
 
• Holds the third-largest forest cover by area in the country, spanning **55,717 square kilometers**.
 
• It is renowned for its high production of **Tendu leaves** and dense **Sal** and **Teak** forests.
 
 
 
• **Mizoram**:
 
 
• While smaller in total area, it leads the country in forest cover by **percentage**, with **84.53%** of its land under forest.
 
 
 
• **Forest Density Classification**:
 
 
• **Very Dense Forest (VDF)**: All lands with tree canopy density of **70%** and above.
 
• **Moderately Dense Forest (MDF)**: All lands with tree canopy density between **40% and 70%**.
 
• **Open Forest (OF)**: All lands with tree canopy density between **10% and 40%**.

questions.question: According to an official notification for scrapping of the 'No-Detention Policy' for Classes 5 and 8, if students fail to clear the annual exams, they will be given additional coaching and an opportunity to take a re-exam within ____ months of the results.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (Amendment) Act, 2019**, was enacted to modify the existing provisions regarding the **No-Detention Policy** under the original **RTE Act, 2009**.
 
• According to the amended **Section 16**, there shall be a regular examination in **Class 5** and **Class 8** at the end of every academic year to assess the learning outcomes of the students.
 
• The notification specifies that if a child fails in the regular examination, they must be provided with **additional coaching** by the school to address their learning gaps.
 
• The law explicitly states that the student will be given an opportunity for a **re-examination** within a period of **two months** from the date of the declaration of the results of the regular examination.
 
• The amendment grants the **appropriate government** (state or union territory) the authority to allow schools to **detain** a child in Class 5 or Class 8 if they fail the re-examination, although they cannot be expelled until they complete **elementary education**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **No-Detention Policy (NDP)**

 
 
• This policy was a hallmark of the **RTE Act, 2009**, which mandated that no child could be held back or expelled from school until the completion of **elementary education** (Class 8).
 
• The primary objective was to reduce the **dropout rate** and eliminate the psychological fear of failure and examinations among children aged **6 to 14 years**.
 
• Critics and various committees, including the **TSR Subramanian Committee** and the **Vasudev Devnani Committee**, observed that the lack of examinations led to a decline in **learning standards** and accountability.
 
 
 
• **Elementary Education Scope**
 
 
• Under the **Indian Constitution** and the **RTE Act**, elementary education refers to the period from **Class 1 to Class 8**.
 
• The **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**, inserted **Article 21-A**, making education a **Fundamental Right** for children.

questions.question:
Which report is NOT published by Transparency International?

I. Democracy Index

II. Corruption Perceptions Index
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Democracy Index** is an annual index that provides a snapshot of the state of democracy worldwide. It is compiled and published by the **Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU)**, which is the research and analysis division of **The Economist Group** based in the **United Kingdom**. Hence, statement I is correct.
 
• The **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI)** is the flagship publication of **Transparency International**. Launched in **1995**, it has become the leading global indicator of public sector corruption, ranking **180 countries and territories** by their perceived levels of **public sector corruption**. Hence, statement II is incorrect.
 
• The **Democracy Index** bases its scores on sixty indicators grouped into five categories: **electoral process and pluralism**, **civil liberties**, **functioning of government**, **political participation**, and **political culture**.
 
• **Transparency International** is an **international non-governmental organization** founded in **1993** and headquartered in **Berlin, Germany**, with the primary goal of combating **global corruption** and preventing criminal activities arising from it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transparency International** also publishes other significant reports including:

 
 
• **Global Corruption Barometer**: The only worldwide public opinion survey on views and experiences of **corruption**.
 
• **Bribe Payers Index**: A report that ranks leading exporting countries by the perceived likelihood of their firms to **bribe public officials** abroad.
 
 
 
• **Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU)**:
 
 
• Established in **1946**, it provides **forecasting** and advisory services through research and analysis, such as monthly country reports and five-year country **economic forecasts**.
 
• It is also well-known for publishing the **Global Liveability Index**, which assesses which **global cities** provide the best or worst living conditions.
